changelog.reason: Baseline entry recorded when the scaffold versioning contract was adopted. Changes before this point are in git history rather than here.

The leak guard no longer lists fixed Gemma turn and tool delimiters. It forbids the served model's own chat-template tokens, read at run time from its tokenizer (forbid_chat_template_tokens), so a template leak is caught for any model family; plain strings that are not model tokens stay in expected_not_contains. An unloadable tokenizer makes the case a harness error.

The description no longer says the two expected_not_contains strings are not tokens of the model: they are checked for every model, whether or not its tokenizer has them as tokens. Wording only; the verdict rules are unchanged.

meta.description: Template-sensitive half of a pair. The conversation is prebuilt so the model is not asked to call anything: an assistant turn already carries a tool_calls block, and a tool turn already carries the answer, keyed back by tool_call_id. The only work left is to read 'QX7R2M' out of that tool turn and say it. The tracking code is deliberately meaningless, so it cannot be recalled from pre-training or inferred from the question, and the only way it reaches the output is if the chat template serialized the tool response into the prompt and closed the tool chain so the model answers instead of calling again. Pair this with template_tool_response_twin, which hands the model the same two values in one plain user turn. Twin passes and this fails means the values are readable and the tool-response serialization is what broke, so look at the chat template. Both fail means the model cannot read a value back at all and the template is not implicated. The forbidden strings catch the other template failure mode, where the serialization scaffolding leaks into the visible answer instead of being consumed by the template. They are the served model's own chat-template tokens (forbid_chat_template_tokens), read at run time from its tokenizer, every special token plus every added token that appears in its chat template (whitespace, one-character and plain-word tokens, which correct answers contain, are left out), so the check covers whatever model family is under test and records the tokens it checked. expected_not_contains adds two plain strings checked for every model, whether or not its tokenizer has them as tokens: tool_call_id (the OpenAI field name; in the answer it means the tool message was echoed as raw JSON) and <tool_response> (a wrapper tag some templates emit). If the tokenizer cannot be loaded the case is a harness error, not a pass. One thing this case does not assert is the wire encoding of tool_calls[].function.arguments, which is a JSON-encoded string here because that is what the OpenAI schema specifies. Servers deserialize it before rendering, and the Gemma 4 template raises if handed the string form directly, so a case file that stored a mapping here would be testing the renderer rather than the endpoint.
